title: Logarithms: The Mathematics of Exponents, Reversed

questions.question: What is the value of log₄ 8?
logₐ 1 equals:
questions.rationale: Any positive base to the power 0 gives 1, so log of 1 in any (valid) base is 0.

questions.question: Which expression equals log(mn)?
questions.rationale: The product law: log(mn) = log m + log n — multiplication of arguments becomes addition of logs (same base).

questions.question: Express log(x⁵) in terms of log x:
questions.rationale: The power law: log(mᵏ) = k·log m, so log(x⁵) = 5 log x.

questions.question: Which of the following is undefined in the real numbers?
questions.rationale: Logarithms require a positive argument: no real power of 10 is negative. log₁₀ 0.001 = −3 is perfectly valid.

questions.question: The change-of-base rule states log_a x equals:
questions.rationale: log_a x = log_b x / log_b a — dividing the two same-base logs isolates the unknown base.

questions.question: An earthquake of magnitude 7 compared to one of magnitude 5 has ground motion amplitude:
questions.rationale: The Richter scale is logarithmic: each unit multiplies amplitude by 10, so two units means 10² = 100 times.
